events.title: Fortran 2003 standard published (ISO/IEC 1539-1:2004)
events.summary: ISO/IEC 1539-1:2004 was published on November 18, 2004 — the Fortran 2003 standard with object-oriented features.
events.about: Fortran 2003 added derived-type OOP, allocatable arrays with full semantics, C interoperability (`ISO_C_BINDING`), and stream I/O. It let Fortran call C libraries directly — critical for linking with modern numerical and GPU stacks without wrapper layers.

narrative.whyChosen: Fortran 2003 brought OOP and C interop — the features HPC codes needed to integrate with the rest of the software stack.
narrative.whyImportant: C binding and improved allocatables made Fortran viable alongside C/C++ in mixed-language supercomputing projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Fortran 95 could not cleanly interoperate with C libraries or express object-oriented models researchers expected.
